back2basics.text: Judicial review allows courts to examine and ensure that laws and policies comply with constitutional rights and justice. The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, decriminalises suicide attempts by presuming severe stress, shifting the burden to prosecution to prove otherwise. Courts can intervene to protect vulnerable individuals, including armed personnel, ensuring their mental health rights and welfare are upheld.

back2basics.text: Health financing refers to how funds are collected, pooled, and spent to provide health services. Out-of-pocket expenditure is the direct payment made by individuals for healthcare services at the time of use, which can cause financial hardship. Reducing out-of-pocket expenditure through increased government spending and insurance schemes improves access and financial protection.

body: Objectives include preventing child marriage, teenage pregnancy, and ensuring health and safety of adolescent girls.
Key measures involve mandatory gynaecological check-ups, sex education, Child Protection Committees, counselling, and CCTV installation.
The policy aims to create safe educational environments, promote awareness of rights, and ensure continued education until age 18.
structure.conclusion: Karnataka's policy reflects a comprehensive approach to adolescent welfare by integrating health, education, and protection measures.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about Karnataka's recent education and health policy for girls:
1. The policy mandates mandatory gynaecological check-ups for all girls in schools.
2. Child Protection Committees in schools must meet once every six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because Child Protection Committees must meet once every three months, not six months.

body.label: Mandatory gynaecological check-ups
body.text: All girls in schools must undergo mandatory check-ups by a gynaecologist to monitor adolescent health.

body.label: Sex education and awareness
body.text: Sex education is mandated, including awareness on child rights, teenage pregnancy, child marriage, POCSO Act, and child helpline 1098.

body.label: Child Protection Committees
body.text: Schools must form Child Protection Committees comprising parents, children, and teachers that meet quarterly to address student welfare.

body.label: CCTV installation and counselling
body.text: Installation of CCTV cameras is compulsory, and qualified counsellors must be appointed to address mental health and abuse issues.

body.label: Legal action for negligence
body.text: Failure to prevent or address child marriage, teenage pregnancy, or POCSO cases will lead to legal and disciplinary action against officials.

sections.heading: What are the key measures mandated by Karnataka for schools and colleges?

body.label: Rising child marriage and teenage pregnancy
body.text: The circular is a response to increasing cases of child marriage and teenage pregnancy in the state.

body.label: Protecting adolescent health and rights
body.text: The measures aim to safeguard adolescent girls' health, prevent abuse, and ensure continued education until age 18.

body.label: Preventing exploitation and abuse
body.text: The policy includes steps to prevent child labour, trafficking, sexual abuse, and substance abuse among students.

sections.heading: Why were these measures introduced by Karnataka?

body.label: Regular meetings and grievance redressal
body.text: Child Protection Committees will meet every three months, and complaint boxes will be installed to address grievances.

body.label: Tracking absenteeism
body.text: If a girl student is absent for more than three days without notice, the principal must inform the gram panchayat and child helpline.

body.label: Counselling and re-enrolment efforts
body.text: Counsellors will address mental health challenges, and teachers must persuade parents to re-enrol girls who dropped out.

body.label: Legal measures against illegal abortion
body.text: The Health Department will take legal action against shops selling abortion pills without prescription and unauthorized abortion providers.

sections.heading: How will the policy be implemented and monitored?
